::: {.cite-bar .domain-aid-sanctions}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 105-277]{.cite} [112 Stat. 2681-761]{.cite} [22 U.S.C. 6501 et seq.]{.cite}
:::

Division G of the FY1999 omnibus appropriations act. It folded the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and the U.S. Information Agency into the State Department and, for the first time, gave USAID a statutory existence as an independent establishment.

## Key provisions

- Abolished the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency and the U.S. Information Agency and moved their functions to State.
- Sec. 1413 (22 U.S.C. 6563): USAID recognized as an independent establishment, with the Administrator under the foreign policy guidance of the Secretary of State.
- Made international broadcasting independent under the Broadcasting Board of Governors.

## Why it matters

It is the statute at the center of the argument over whether a President can dissolve or absorb USAID without Congress. It also explains why public diplomacy under the [Smith-Mundt Act](smith-mundt-1948.qmd) sits inside State, and it amended the [State Basic Authorities Act](state-basic-1956.qmd).

## Current status

In force. In 2025 the administration moved USAID's remaining functions into the State Department and wound down most of the agency without new legislation; the statutory provisions on the agency have not been repealed and the action has been litigated. Check current status.
